He Lost His Mother on 9/11. He Grew Up in Her Childhood Bedroom.
I met Jake Campbell years ago, after I read a story about his challenges since his mother died on Sept. 11. I messaged him on Facebook, and we stayed in touch.
Jake, just 25, wants to overcome the ache he feels for the mother he barely knew. His 85-year-old grandmother Jeanne Maurer, who raised him, clings to grief as a connection to her daughter.
After joining them at Ground Zero for the 9/11 anniversary last year and attending Jake’s Dartmouth graduation in June, I asked if they would talk to me for a story about grief.
I thought I knew Jake and Jeanne before this story. But with a notebook between us, we had incredibly intimate conversations about sorrow, faith and healing that changed me.
